title: the analytics lifecycle and data-driven decision making
question: What is the correct order of the six stages in the analytics lifecycle?
options: Data Collection, Business Question, Analysis, Data Preparation, Communication, Interpretation|Business Question, Data Collection, Data Preparation, Analysis, Interpretation, Communication|Business Question, Analysis, Data Collection, Interpretation, Data Preparation, Communication|Data Preparation, Data Collection, Business Question, Analysis, Communication, Interpretation
answer: Business Question, Data Collection, Data Preparation, Analysis, Interpretation, Communication

title: the analytics lifecycle and data-driven decision making
question: Which stage of the analytics lifecycle involves turning a vague concern such as "delivery is bad" into a specific, answerable question?
options: Data Preparation|Analysis|Business Question|Communication
answer: Business Question

title: the analytics lifecycle and data-driven decision making
question: Which of the following best describes the Data Preparation stage?
options: Gathering the data needed to answer the question|Cleaning and organising raw data so it is fit for analysis|Deciding what the numbers mean for the business|Presenting a finding so the right person can act on it
answer: Cleaning and organising raw data so it is fit for analysis

title: the analytics lifecycle and data-driven decision making
question: A colleague asks you to remove duplicate rows from the delivery log before any calculations are done. Which lifecycle stage does this task belong to?
options: Business Question|Data Preparation|Interpretation|Communication
answer: Data Preparation

title: the analytics lifecycle and data-driven decision making
question: A manager asks: "Are late deliveries getting better or worse this quarter?" Formulating and sharpening this request into something answerable represents which stage?
options: Business Question|Analysis|Data Collection|Interpretation
answer: Business Question

title: the analytics lifecycle and data-driven decision making
question: You use a spreadsheet formula to calculate the average delay per branch from the cleaned delivery log. Which stage are you performing?
options: Data Collection|Data Preparation|Analysis|Communication
answer: Analysis

title: the analytics lifecycle and data-driven decision making
question: You send a one-page summary to the operations manager recommending a dispatch-process review for the Ikeja branch. Which stage is this?
options: Analysis|Interpretation|Communication|Data Collection
answer: Communication

title: the analytics lifecycle and data-driven decision making
question: Ikeja's average delay is calculated as 2.3 days, nearly double every other branch. Stating that this is driving most of last month's complaints and is worth investigating first belongs to which stage?
options: Analysis|Interpretation|Data Collection|Business Question
answer: Interpretation

title: the analytics lifecycle and data-driven decision making
question: Why is the analytics lifecycle better represented as a loop rather than a straight line?
options: Because each stage must be repeated exactly twice before moving on|Because a communicated insight often produces a new business question, restarting the cycle|Because Data Collection and Data Preparation are actually the same stage|Because Analysis always comes before Data Collection in practice
answer: Because a communicated insight often produces a new business question, restarting the cycle

title: the analytics lifecycle and data-driven decision making
question: A team produces a chart of branch delay averages and hands it to a manager with no accompanying explanation of why it matters or what to do next. Which stage was most likely skipped?
options: Data Collection|Data Preparation|Interpretation|Business Question
answer: Interpretation

title: data types, data structures and the data team
question: In the delivery log, which column is an example of numerical data?
options: branch|delay_days|complaint_notes|delivery_partner
answer: delay_days

title: data types, data structures and the data team
question: Which column in the delivery log is best described as categorical data?
options: delay_days|order_value_naira|branch|dispatch_date
answer: branch

title: data types, data structures and the data team
question: What is the key difference between structured and unstructured data?
options: Structured data is always numerical, unstructured data is always text|Structured data fits neatly into rows and columns, unstructured data has no fixed row-and-column shape|Structured data is stored on paper, unstructured data is stored digitally|Structured data cannot be analysed, unstructured data can always be analysed directly
answer: Structured data fits neatly into rows and columns, unstructured data has no fixed row-and-column shape

title: data types, data structures and the data team
question: The delivery log's order_id column is made up entirely of digits. Why is it best classified as categorical rather than numerical?
options: Because it is stored as text in the file|Because you would never meaningfully average or sum two order IDs|Because it always starts with the letters "ORD"|Because it is the first column in the file
answer: Because you would never meaningfully average or sum two order IDs

title: data types, data structures and the data team
question: A new column, customer_rating (1 to 5 stars), is added to the delivery log. What data type is it?
options: Numerical, continuous|Text|Categorical, ordinal (it has a natural order)|Date/time
answer: Categorical, ordinal (it has a natural order)

title: data types, data structures and the data team
question: The delivery log's complaint_notes column sits inside a structured CSV file. How should its content best be described?
options: Structured, because the file itself is structured|Unstructured in content, even though it sits inside a structured file|Numerical, because it is a column in a spreadsheet|Date/time, because complaints are logged over time
answer: Unstructured in content, even though it sits inside a structured file

title: data types, data structures and the data team
question: Which data team role is primarily responsible for building and maintaining the pipelines that collect and store data?
options: Data analyst|Data engineer|Business intelligence developer|Data governance officer
answer: Data engineer

title: data types, data structures and the data team
question: In a small Nigerian fintech, one person single-handedly collects, cleans, analyses and reports on data. Which established data-team roles are most closely being combined in this situation?
options: Data governance officer and business intelligence developer only|Data engineer and data analyst, and often elements of BI reporting|Data scientist only, since all data work is inherently predictive modelling|No roles are being combined, since one person cannot perform more than one role
answer: Data engineer and data analyst, and often elements of BI reporting

title: data types, data structures and the data team
question: Two columns both contain only digits: order_id and delay_days. What is the best explanation for why only one of them is treated as numerical data?
options: delay_days has fewer unique values than order_id|order_id is an identifier that is never meaningfully summed or averaged, while delay_days represents a measurable quantity|order_id is always longer than delay_days|Numerical data must always be a whole number, and both columns are whole numbers, so both are numerical
answer: order_id is an identifier that is never meaningfully summed or averaged, while delay_days represents a measurable quantity

title: data types, data structures and the data team
question: Which statement most accurately distinguishes the data analyst's role from the data scientist's role on a data team?
options: The analyst only writes code, while the data scientist never writes code|The analyst cleans, explores and interprets data to answer business questions and communicate findings, while the data scientist builds predictive models and deeper statistical work|The analyst and data scientist perform identical tasks in every organisation|The data scientist reports to the analyst in every data team structure
answer: The analyst cleans, explores and interprets data to answer business questions and communicate findings, while the data scientist builds predictive models and deeper statistical work

question: Which tool in the programme toolkit is used for running real code in notebooks, rather than for chat-based conversation?
options: Claude|ChatGPT|Google Colab|Gemini
answer: Google Colab

title: the ai-augmented analyst and toolkit setup
question: According to this topic, what is one thing that genuinely changes for an analyst who uses AI tools?
options: The analyst no longer needs to verify any answer|Drafting speed and first-pass code, formulas or summaries become faster|The business question no longer needs to be defined|AI tools remove the need for a data team entirely
answer: Drafting speed and first-pass code, formulas or summaries become faster

title: the ai-augmented analyst and toolkit setup
question: Which category of information must never be pasted into an AI tool, according to this topic?
options: The names of the four toolkit assistants|Real customer or colleague personal data|The column headers of a safe, prepared dataset|A business question written in your own words
answer: Real customer or colleague personal data

title: the ai-augmented analyst and toolkit setup
question: A trainee pastes the order_value_naira column into a chatbot as plain text, with currency symbols and commas left in, and asks for the total. Based on this topic's hook exercise, what is the most likely outcome?
options: The assistant will always refuse to respond|The assistant may confidently state an incorrect total that must be checked against the real sum|The assistant will automatically remove the currency symbols and calculate correctly every time|The spreadsheet total will change to match the assistant's answer
answer: The assistant may confidently state an incorrect total that must be checked against the real sum

title: the ai-augmented analyst and toolkit setup
description: What stays the same with AI
question: Which statement correctly reflects what does NOT change about the analyst's job when AI tools are introduced?
options: The analyst no longer needs to understand the business context|The analyst still owns the business question and must verify the AI's output before trusting it|The analyst can skip the Data Preparation stage entirely|The analyst's communication stage becomes automatic
answer: The analyst still owns the business question and must verify the AI's output before trusting it

title: the ai-augmented analyst and toolkit setup
question: A trainee has already calculated branch delay averages in a spreadsheet and wants an assistant to suggest follow-up questions worth investigating. Which is the most appropriate use of the assistant here?
options: Ask it to recalculate the averages from scratch to double-check the spreadsheet|Ask it to suggest questions to investigate further, then filter which ones are answerable from the real data|Ask it to replace the spreadsheet entirely for all future calculations|Ask it to decide which branch should be investigated without any human review
answer: Ask it to suggest questions to investigate further, then filter which ones are answerable from the real data

title: the ai-augmented analyst and toolkit setup
question: Which toolkit component would be most useful if a trainee's work already lives in Google Sheets or Google Docs?
options: Google Colab|Claude|Gemini|publica.academy
answer: Gemini

title: the ai-augmented analyst and toolkit setup
question: A pair of trainees ask an assistant to count the unique branches in the delivery log and receive an incorrect count. What does this best illustrate?
options: That counting tasks are too advanced for any AI assistant|That a confident AI answer can still be wrong, so verification is required even for simple-looking tasks|That the delivery log itself must be corrupted|That only complex calculations, never simple ones, need to be verified
answer: That a confident AI answer can still be wrong, so verification is required even for simple-looking tasks

title: the ai-augmented analyst and toolkit setup
question: Why does the programme insist on teaching the traditional, non-AI method of a skill before the AI-assisted version, rather than teaching the AI-assisted method alone?
options: Because AI tools are unreliable and should never be used in practice|So the analyst can operate without AI tools and is equipped to judge whether the AI's output is actually correct|Because traditional methods are always faster than AI-assisted methods|Because the programme's software licences do not permit AI tools in early weeks
answer: So the analyst can operate without AI tools and is equipped to judge whether the AI's output is actually correct

title: the ai-augmented analyst and toolkit setup
question: A trainee's assistant, when asked to sum a currency column, returns a total that does not match the spreadsheet's SUM formula. Based on the topic's hook exercise, what is the most likely underlying cause?
options: The spreadsheet formula is broken and the assistant's answer should be trusted instead|Currency symbols and commas left in the pasted text were most likely misread when the assistant processed the values|The assistant deliberately gives wrong answers to test the trainee|Spreadsheets cannot calculate totals correctly, only AI assistants can
answer: Currency symbols and commas left in the pasted text were most likely misread when the assistant processed the values

title: prompt fundamentals for data work
question: What are the four ingredients of a good data prompt, as taught in this topic?
options: Context, Data description, Task, Output format|Greeting, Question, Apology, Closing|Data description, Output format, Signature, Deadline|Context, Opinion, Task, Conclusion
answer: Context, Data description, Task, Output format

title: prompt fundamentals for data work
question: Which prompt ingredient tells the assistant what the dataset actually contains, since it usually cannot see your spreadsheet directly?
options: Context|Data description|Task|Output format
answer: Data description

title: prompt fundamentals for data work
question: Which prompt ingredient states exactly how you want the answer structured, such as a table or a short list?
options: Context|Task|Output format|Data description
answer: Output format

title: prompt fundamentals for data work
question: A trainee writes the prompt "Look at the delays." Compared to a stronger version like "Calculate the average delay_days per branch and identify the branch with the highest average," which ingredient is the weak prompt missing precision on?
options: Context|Task|Output format|Data description
answer: Task

title: prompt fundamentals for data work
question: Which of these best demonstrates including a data description in a prompt?
options: "You are helping a Lagos logistics firm."|"Here is a delivery log with columns order_id, dispatch_date, delivery_date, branch and delay_days, 400 rows."|"Return the result as a table sorted from highest to lowest."|"Please help me."
answer: "Here is a delivery log with columns order_id, dispatch_date, delivery_date, branch and delay_days, 400 rows."

title: prompt fundamentals for data work
question: A trainee's first prompt attempt returns a long, unstructured paragraph instead of something directly usable. Which ingredient, if added, would most directly fix this?
options: Context|Data description|Output format|Task
answer: Output format

title: prompt fundamentals for data work
question: What is the correct action to take when a prompt returns a poor first answer?
options: Assume the task is impossible and abandon the prompt entirely|Diagnose which ingredient was thin or missing, sharpen it, and re-run the prompt|Repeat the exact same prompt several times until the answer changes|Switch to a different assistant without changing the prompt at all
answer: Diagnose which ingredient was thin or missing, sharpen it, and re-run the prompt

title: prompt fundamentals for data work
question: Iteration 1 of a prompt has no context or format and returns a generic answer. Iteration 2 adds data description and task, and returns a long unstructured paragraph. Iteration 3 adds output format and returns a clean, verifiable table. What does this progression best demonstrate?
options: That only the first ingredient added ever matters|Iterative prompt refinement, where each added ingredient measurably improves the usability of the answer|That assistants become less accurate the more detail you give them|That output format is the only ingredient that ever matters
answer: Iterative prompt refinement, where each added ingredient measurably improves the usability of the answer

title: prompt fundamentals for data work
question: Why is receiving a poor first answer from an AI assistant considered a normal part of the workflow rather than a sign of failure?
options: Because AI assistants are designed to always give a wrong answer first|Because a poor answer usually reflects one missing or unclear ingredient, not an impossible question|Because trainees are expected to give up after the first attempt|Because the programme discourages re-running any prompt more than once
answer: Because a poor answer usually reflects one missing or unclear ingredient, not an impossible question

title: prompt fundamentals for data work
question: A trainee's prompt already includes clear context and a precise task, but the assistant still returns a wrong total for a currency column. Drawing on both Topic 3 and Topic 4, what is the most likely remaining fix?
options: Remove the task ingredient entirely, since it is not needed|Improve the data description to flag currency symbols or commas in the values, and still verify the output against the spreadsheet|Assume the answer is correct, since context and task were already strong|Switch the output format to a paragraph instead of a table
answer: Improve the data description to flag currency symbols or commas in the values, and still verify the output against the spreadsheet

title: verification habits and responsible use
question: Which of the following best defines "verification" of an AI-produced answer?
options: Deciding the answer looks reasonable and moving on|Checking the answer against something you trust more than the AI's confidence, such as a manual calculation|Asking a second AI assistant the same question and comparing tone|Assuming the answer is correct if it was returned quickly
answer: Checking the answer against something you trust more than the AI's confidence, such as a manual calculation

title: verification habits and responsible use
question: Which of the following counts as an acceptable verification method for an AI-produced answer?
options: "It looks right"|Recalculating the result independently and comparing it|Trusting the answer because it was stated confidently|Assuming the answer is correct because the assistant is usually reliable
answer: Recalculating the result independently and comparing it

title: verification habits and responsible use
question: Which category of data must never be entered into an AI tool, according to this topic?
options: Column headers from a safely prepared dataset|Real customer names, phone numbers or addresses|A business question written in the analyst's own words|A branch name such as "Ikeja"
answer: Real customer names, phone numbers or addresses

title: verification habits and responsible use
question: An assistant claims "Ikeja's average delay is 2.3 days, the highest of the three branches." Given that this is a low-effort, high-stakes number that will drive a business recommendation, which verification method fits best?
options: Cross-reference against an unrelated report|Recalculate the average directly from the prepared data|Accept the claim since it matches expectations|Ask a different assistant to repeat the same claim
answer: Recalculate the average directly from the prepared data

title: verification habits and responsible use
question: Which of the three verification methods involves comparing an AI-produced answer against a separate, already-trusted source, such as an earlier report?
options: Recalculate|Spot-check|Cross-reference|Disclose
answer: Cross-reference

title: verification habits and responsible use
question: A manager asks a trainee to paste a real customer complaint log, including names and phone numbers, into an assistant to summarise common issues. What should the trainee do?
options: Paste the file as requested, since the manager approved it|Decline to paste the raw file, explain why, and propose an anonymised alternative|Paste only the phone numbers, since names are the more sensitive field|Proceed, but only using a personal AI account instead of the company one
answer: Decline to paste the raw file, explain why, and propose an anonymised alternative

title: verification habits and responsible use
question: Under the Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA), why can pasting real customer data into a public AI tool be a problem?
options: Because AI tools are always slower than manual analysis|Because it may count as an unauthorised transfer of personal data to a third party|Because AI tools cannot process any text data|Because the NDPA only applies to government agencies, not analysts
answer: Because it may count as an unauthorised transfer of personal data to a third party

title: verification habits and responsible use
question: A claim states "The delivery log shows 400 total orders," but the actual raw file contains 412 rows, including 12 exact duplicates. What does this best illustrate about verification?
options: That row counts never need to be checked, only averages do|That a stated figure should be checked directly against the file rather than trusted, since duplicates or other quirks can make a raw count differ from a clean one|That the delivery log is unusable once any duplicates are present|That duplicates always increase the average delay, so no verification is needed
answer: That a stated figure should be checked directly against the file rather than trusted, since duplicates or other quirks can make a raw count differ from a clean one

title: verification habits and responsible use
question: Why is data protection described as a professional duty resting with the individual analyst, rather than only with the employer's policy?
options: Because employers are never responsible for data protection under any circumstance|Because analysts routinely handle the personal data that other roles collect, so responsibility for safe use sits with whoever is handling it at that moment|Because only senior managers are covered by the NDPA|Because personal data protection only applies once data leaves the company's building
answer: Because analysts routinely handle the personal data that other roles collect, so responsibility for safe use sits with whoever is handling it at that moment

title: verification habits and responsible use
question: Which best explains why delivery_log.csv is safe to paste into an AI tool throughout the programme?
options: Because it is a small file, and small files are always safe|Because real personal identifiers were removed or replaced with generated values before it was distributed to trainees|Because it is only used internally within the programme|Because AI tools cannot read CSV files, so no data is actually shared
answer: Because real personal identifiers were removed or replaced with generated values before it was distributed to trainees
